name: Citizenship by Naturalization

requirements.blocker_text: The last confirmed, publicly translated Afghan nationality framework (the 1936 Nationality Law) allowed naturalization after 5 years of continuous residence OR service to the government, provided the applicant had reached legal majority, had no criminal record in Afghanistan, and posed no apparent threat to national security. A 2015 amendment effort to update the nationality statute began but was not confirmed completed as of the last available update (2017), and no Taliban-era nationality law has been identified since the 2021 takeover -- the administration's Justice Ministry stated in September 2021 that governance would proceed under the 1964 Constitution's Sharia-compliant provisions pending a new constitution, but no confirmation was found that this specifically addresses naturalization procedure. This route is modeled on the last confirmed legal text, with that uncertainty disclosed rather than presented as settled current law.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of continuous residence (or documented government service), maintain a clean record, and apply -- noting that the current administration's actual processing practice for this route could not be confirmed.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous residence (or government service record)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 5 years continuous residence (last confirmed pre-2021 standard)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Afghanistan). STATUS: DRAFT -- best available primary text is a UN-hosted translation of a 1936 law (tier 2), with no post-2021 Taliban nationality statute confirmed to exist in any source reached during this build; the strongest disclosure across every Afghanistan file is that 'since the Taliban took control of the country in 2021, it is unclear what laws are in place' for nationality specifically. GENUINE, SEPARATE FINDING carried here rather than in a standalone marriage file: the 1932 law that automatically granted/stripped Afghan nationality on marriage was repealed by the 1986 law, which made nationality gender-neutral and marriage-independent -- meaning there is NO confirmed accelerated citizenship-by-marriage track in Afghanistan today (a foreign spouse of an Afghan citizen would use this standard naturalization route, with no reduced residency period found), a genuine absence rather than an asymmetry, comparable to Haiti's finding earlier in this dataset. No inbound family-reunification residency mechanism for a foreign spouse/relative of an Afghan citizen was found in this build either -- every reachable source concerned Afghans reuniting with family abroad (post-2021 evacuation programs), not foreigners joining family inside Afghanistan; this dataset does not fabricate a mechanism to fill that gap, and no family_reunification.json was created for this country as a result. dual_citizenship_allowed left null: permitted since 2001 in practice, but the still-technically-unrepealed 1986 law prohibited it, and the 2004 Constitution bars only the presidency from dual nationality, with no post-2021 confirmation of current practice found.
